chunks: We said: If this conclusion were to be inferred from us, it would also be inferred from all the followers of justice by the view of the atheists, when they say, 'We reach the conclusion that its Doer is not wise through these actions which are not apparent in wisdom,' because if He were wise, you would have been able to explain the aspect of wisdom in them; otherwise, what is the distinction?

key_terms.الْمُلِحَدَة: Atheists / Those who attribute no wisdom

ai.seo_question: How does the argument from divine wisdom apply to atheists and followers of justice?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi employs a *qiyas* (analogical reasoning) to defend the doctrine of Occultation (*Ghayba*) by demonstrating that the absence of apparent wisdom (*hikmah zahirah*) is not a unique flaw of the Shia position but a universal condition accepted even by monotheists and atheists. This passage highlights the Shia epistemological stance that divine wisdom is often hidden from human perception, thereby validating the Occultation as a logical consequence of God's absolute wisdom rather than a contradiction to it. It underscores the scholarly principle that the lack of immediate, observable rationale does not negate the existence of profound, underlying divine purposes.
